extracted.intended_audience: general readers and public-relations/communications professionals interested in crisis communications
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluate a corporation's crisis public-relations response (case study of BP Deepwater Horizon) and extract actionable standards for effective crisis communications and reputation management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state that the company is accountable for the disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The public needed to hear that BP was accountable for the disaster; failing to accept responsibility was a primary PR failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express deep concern and empathy for harm caused
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate genuine concern for people affected and convey empathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be humble and conciliatory; apologize early. Anti-pattern: 'hiding behind the lawyers' or sounding callous (example: executives who didn't apologize).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a clear, realistic plan of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell stakeholders what will be done next and what steps are underway to address the problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid false assurances. Instead of slogans like 'We will get this done, we will make this right' while the problem remains uncontrolled, say 'We're doing everything we can to get it under control.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Be honest about what is not under control
rubrics_metrics.description: Admit limitations and uncertainties rather than covering up or denying facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should have been prepared to admit they didn't have it under control; denying scientific evidence (e.g., large plumes) undermines credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose an appropriate spokesperson
rubrics_metrics.description: Use spokespeople who understand the media and public perception and who will not make damaging gaffes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid putting a CEO with poor media instincts and insensitive comments in front of the public; replace ineffective faces promptly (example: criticism of Tony Hayward and later replacement with Bob Dudley).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain sufficient internal public- and government-relations capacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep experienced, in-house PR/government-relations staff rather than cutting them to save costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cuts to BP's PR and government-relations shop left executives listening to outside consultants and rookies, contributing to poor decisions (e.g., walking beaches in a starched white shirt).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deflecting blame
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not immediately blame contractors or others; avoid statements implying the incident is 'not our accident.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early declarations that shifted blame made the company look arrogant and callous and damaged trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid tone-deaf advertising and slogans during an ongoing crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Be careful with campaign messaging; slogans can backfire if they promise control or fixes that aren't yet achieved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ad 'We will get this done, we will make this right' was criticized as inappropriate while the well was still gushing; such messaging can sound like false reassurance to affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use social media proactively to inform and listen
rubrics_metrics.description: Set up social channels to provide timely updates, technical briefings, and to hear public sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BP quickly ramped up social media (YouTube, Facebook, Twitter); posting detailed technical briefings helped public understanding and letting people vent showed BP was listening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor media and correct misinformation in real time
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuously watch traditional and social media and use channels to promptly correct errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: BP's team told a CNN producer to read a recent tweet to correct an on-air mistake; real-time social corrections can shape coverage immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage local, culturally credible messengers
rubrics_metrics.description: Deploy representatives who share local roots or cultural ties to affected communities to build trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BP sent a Louisiana native, Glenn DaGian, to meet fishermen and locals; his accent and background helped him connect and persuade in ways outsiders could not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish credible remedial and compensation mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Create transparent, independent compensation and remediation processes to address harms and rebuild trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BP's creation of an independent $20 billion compensation fund and ads featuring Gulf Coast natives were steps that helped, even if reputation remained damaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid minimizing or denying scientific/technical findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept and communicate scientific evidence (e.g., extent of pollution) rather than denying or downplaying it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denying the existence of large oil plumes or scientific findings further erodes credibility; be transparent about technical realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to change strategy and personnel when response fails
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize when an approach or spokesperson is causing harm and make timely course corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BP's board took too long to realize Hayward was the wrong choice; faster adjustments can limit reputational damage.
